paragraphs.text: Prothrombin (factor II) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive coagulation disorder. Meeks and Abshire (2008) estimated that it occurs in about 1 in 1 to 2 million people, and Akhavan et al. (2000) described it as associated with a moderately severe bleeding tendency. Lancellotti and De Cristofaro (2009) distinguished 2 main phenotypes. Hypoprothrombinemia (type I deficiency) shows low prothrombin activity and low antigen levels together. Dysprothrombinemia (type II deficiency) shows normal or near-normal synthesis of a dysfunctional protein. Some compound heterozygotes have hypoprothrombinemia together with dysprothrombinemia. Lefkowitz et al. (2000) described dysprothrombinemia as a rare congenital cause of bleeding and noted that fewer than 25 families with a functional prothrombin defect had been reported.

paragraphs.text: In a review, Girolami et al. (1998) stated that bleeding may be severe in homozygous true deficiency, in which hemarthroses and intracranial bleeding have been described. Bleeding is more variable in the dysprothrombinemias, and heterozygotes are usually asymptomatic. Prognosis generally follows the level of prothrombin activity. The hypoprothrombinemia allele was a 1-bp insertion of T at position 4177 in exon 6 of the F2 gene. checks.evidence_quote: In this study, 13 patients with prothrombin deficiency were screened for the presence of alterations in the prothrombin gene, and nine novel candidate mutations were identified.
checks.explanation: The abstract states that 13 patients were screened and 9 novel mutations were found.

checks.claim: Akhavan et al. (2000) identified an arg538-to-cys substitution in the catalytic serine protease domain of prothrombin in a patient with prothrombin deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: the catalytic serine protease domain (Gly330Ser, Ser354Arg. Arg382His and Arg538Cys)
checks.explanation: The abstract places Arg538Cys in the catalytic serine protease domain.

paragraphs.text: Akhavan et al. (2000) identified a 3-bp in-frame deletion in the F2 gene that removes 1 amino acid (del lys301/302). It was 1 of 9 novel mutations found in a study of 13 patients with prothrombin deficiency.
